# Proposal

I plan to compare the risk and return profiles of six investment assets over the past ten years (Jan 1, 2016 – Dec 31, 2025): VOO (S&P 500), QQQ (NASDAQ-100), IWM (Russell 2000), VTI (total U.S. market), GLD (gold), and BTC-USD (Bitcoin). My motivation is to quantify how much diversification benefit alternative assets like gold and Bitcoin actually provide alongside standard equity holdings, and whether higher-risk assets have historically delivered proportionally higher risk-adjusted returns. I will combine two data source types:
(1) an API source — daily adjusted closing prices pulled from Yahoo Finance via the tidyquant package in R for the six tickers;
(2) a CSV source — FRED's monthly CPI (CPIAUCSL) and daily 3-month Treasury rate (DGS3MO), used for inflation-adjusted returns and as the risk-free rate in Sharpe ratio calculations.

The workflow will follow acquire → tidy → transform → analyze → present in R/RMarkdown: converting prices to log returns, joining the macro data, then producing a growth-of-$1 chart, a correlation heatmap, and a summary table of annualized return, volatility, and Sharpe ratio by asset. As a feature beyond class, I'll compute rolling 12-month correlations to show how diversification relationships shift over time.
